content.title: Open the in-page security modal from the preview
content.intent: Prove OPEN SECURITY in the preview opens the in-page modal and the modal shows the required security detail sections.
content.technique_notes: Techniques: state_flow for the preview-to-modal transition; equivalence partitioning for the OPEN SECURITY action as the modal-entry class. strength=2 by risk judgement because no money, auth, or data-loss factors apply; no covering-array sweep was needed because this path varies by a single entry action.

content.title: Open a security preview by explicit ticker activation
content.intent: Prove explicit ticker activation opens the preview popover with security details without reflowing the page.
content.technique_notes: Techniques: equivalence partitioning over preview-entry modes, with explicit activation treated as a distinct interaction class from hover. strength=2 by risk judgement because no money, auth, or data-loss factors apply; no covering-array sweep was needed because the path has one varying input class.

content.title: Close the security modal with Escape
content.intent: Prove the open security modal closes when Escape is used.
content.technique_notes: Techniques: state_flow for the modal-open to modal-closed transition; equivalence partitioning over supported dismissal methods, with Escape kept separate because the PRD names it as an independent close route. strength=2 by risk judgement because no money, auth, or data-loss factors apply; no covering-array sweep was needed because the path varies by one dismissal method.

content.title: Click inside the security modal body without closing it
content.intent: Prove clicking inside the modal body does not dismiss the open security modal.
content.technique_notes: Techniques: negative testing for an interaction that must not dismiss the modal; state_flow for preserving the modal-open state after an in-body click. strength=2 by risk judgement because no money, auth, or data-loss factors apply; no covering-array sweep was needed because the path varies by one disallowed interaction.

content.title: Review the default top holdings table
content.intent: Prove the holdings card presents the expected eight holdings rows and the required table columns on the dashboard.
content.technique_notes: Techniques: equivalence partitioning over the default holdings-card state, verifying the named row set and required columns as one read-only presentation class. strength=2 by risk judgement because no money, auth, or data-loss factors apply; no covering-array sweep was needed because there is no multi-input combination space in the cited default-state content.

judgements.rationale: [applicability] Applied equivalence partitioning because the PRD names distinct interaction classes for reaching the preview and dismissing the modal. Applied state_flow to modal-open and modal-close paths because those promises are transitions between visible overlay states. Applied negative testing to the in-body click promise because the PRD explicitly states a non-dismissal behavior that must be preserved.

[applicability] Did not apply boundary value analysis, overflow/underflow, pagination, persistence, CRUD, idempotency, concurrency, currency, notification, temporal, auth, API-contract, responsiveness, i18n, or mobile-native profiles because the cited source for this use-case describes a read-only web dashboard overlay interaction with no numeric input bounds, list paging, persisted mutation, role gate, API surface, locale behavior, or native-app surface promise.
